meta.title: Visit the Gurukul · Ved Vidyalaya Foundation
meta.description: Visitors are welcome at the dawn recitation and the midday meal. How to plan a visit, what to expect, how to reach us, and ways to volunteer or teach.

hero.h1: Come and stand in it at six in the morning.
hero.lede: No page can do what one morning in the Gurukul does. Visitors are welcome at the dawn recitation and at the midday meal. Write to us a week ahead and we will arrange the rest.

items.title: The dawn recitation
items.body: Arrive while it is still dark. Sit at the edge of the verandah. The Gāyatrī first, then two hours of Veda pāṭha with the ācārya. Most visitors say nothing for a long time afterwards.

items.title: The midday meal
items.body: Cooked by the students, eaten together on the floor. Guests are served first. You will be asked, kindly, to finish what is on your plate.

items.title: Write a week ahead
items.body: So that someone is free to receive you and the kitchen knows how many to cook for.

items.title: Dress simply
items.body: Modest, comfortable clothes. Shoes come off at the verandah.

items.title: Bring nothing
items.body: Gifts for the students are gently declined. If you would like to give, the Gurukul will tell you how.

items.title: Ask before photographing
items.body: The students are children, and the recitation is a prayer. Most of the time the answer is yes.

contact.lede: A person replies, usually within a day or two. Please be patient during examinations and festivals.

involved.kicker: Ways to be part of it

items.title: Teach, for a week or a year
items.body: English, mathematics, science, computing. A teacher who stays a while changes what the students believe is possible. Write and tell us what you can offer.

items.title: Volunteer
items.body: The kitchen, the garden, the library, repairs before the monsoon. There is always a job that needs a pair of hands and no special skill.

items.title: Give
items.body: Any amount, once or every month, by UPI or bank transfer. It arrives whole and becomes meals, lamps and lessons.
